Only the first two take affixes. Verbs are always marked for person and number and may also take [[dative]], [[reciprocal (grammar)|reciprocal]], [[reflexive verb|reflexive]], and/or [[instrumental]] markers as well as mode markers, the object specifier, and auxiliaries. They are at or immediately before the end of clauses. All nominal affixes may also be used with verbs, but nouns use a subset of the verbal affixes. They may not use dative, reciprocal, reflexive, or instrumental markers, or mode markers, or auxiliaries. Particles serve many functions, including noun phrase marking and acting as adverbials. ==== Inflection ==== ===== Nouns ===== Nouns may be inflectable or, as most are, non-inflectable. The former group inflects for person and number. It contains names of body parts and kin terms, which must inflect, and a few other personal possessions, with optional inflection. The person markers are {{lang|bll|nk-}} for the first person, {{lang|bll|ay-}} for the second person, and {{lang|bll|Ø-}} for the third person. They may be pluralized with the marker {{lang|bll|-tu}}. The noun's number itself is not marked explicitly. Examples of inflected nouns are below: : {{lang|bll|dodi}} ("throat") → {{lang|bll|ndodi}} ("my throat"), {{lang|bll|idodi}} ("your throat"), {{lang|bll|doxtu}} ("their throats") : {{lang|bll|adi}} ("father") → {{lang|bll|iyadi}} ("your father"), {{lang|bll|nkaxtu}} ("our father") Here are examples of optionally inflected nouns: : {{lang|bll|ti~ati}} ("house") → {{lang|bll|nkti}}/{{lang|bll|nkati}} ("my house") : {{lang|bll|doxpe}} ("shirt") → {{lang|bll|idoxpe}} ("your shirt") Personal pronouns are formed by inflecting the root {{lang|bll|indi}} for person and number. (It may also have been done once by the demonstratives {{lang|bll|he}} and {{lang|bll|de}}.) Pronouns are always optional and emphasized. Singular pronouns may occur as the subject or the object, but the plurals are always subjects (see {{lang|bll|-daha}}). {| class="wikitable" |+ Biloxi pronouns | {{lang|bll|nkindi}} ("I") | {{lang|bll|nkįxtu}} ("we") |- | {{lang|bll|ayindi}} ("you") | {{lang|bll|ayįxtu}} ("you all") |- | {{lang|bll|indi}}{{efn|In [[free variation]] with {{lang|bll|ind}} and {{lang|bll|int}} before {{lang|bll|h}}.}} ("he, she, it") | {{lang|bll|įxtu}}{{efn|In free variation with {{lang|bll|įxt}} before {{lang|bll|h}}.}} ("they") |} Biloxi has two common demonstratives: {{lang|bll|de}} ("this") and {{lang|bll|he}} ("that"). Classificatory verbs specify the subject's position (sitting, standing, etc.) and differ from normal verbs in that the first person is not inflected for person. Inflection for person and number is identical to inflected nouns: : {{lang|bll|nk-}} 1st person : {{lang|bll|ay-}} 2nd person : {{lang|bll|Ø-}} 3rd person : {{lang|bll|-tu}} pluralizes referent of prefix (not used for inanimate subjects) Because of the rules determining the surface manifestations of some combinations of person markers, 2nd-person-on-1st and 3rd-person-on-1st forms are identical, e.g. {{lang|bll|yaxtedi}} ("you hit me, he hit me"). Also, 2nd-person-subj., 2nd-person-on-3rd, and 3rd-person-on-2nd are identical; for example, {{lang|bll|idǫhi'}} ("you see" / you see him" / "they see you"). {{lang|bll|-tu}} marks animate plurality (except with some motion verbs). : {{lang|bll|įkcatu ni}} ("we have not forgotten you") : {{lang|bll|nkyehǫtu ni}} ("we did not know") However, {{lang|bll|-tu}} is not used: # In the presence of the plural auxiliary {{lang|bll|yuke}} ("are"): #: {{lang|bll|dǫhi yuke}} ("they were looking at it") # When the sentence has already been marked as plural: #: {{lang|bll|aditu ką, hidedi nedi}} ("they climbed up, and were falling continually") # If it is followed by a plural motion verb: #: {{lang|bll|dą kahi hą}} ("they took it and were returning") Some (but not all) verbs of motion mark plurality with the prefix {{lang|bll|a-}} inserted directly before the root: : {{lang|bll|de}} ("he goes") → {{lang|bll|nk'''a'''de}} ("we go"), {{lang|bll|ay'''a'''de}} ("you (pl.) go"), {{lang|bll|'''a'''de}} ("they go") : {{lang|bll|kide}} ("he goes homeward") → {{lang|bll|xk'''a'''de}} ("we go homeward") But there are counterexamples (even ones derived from the same roots): : {{lang|bll|kade}} ("he goes thither") → {{lang|bll|xkade'''tu'''}} ("we go thither"), {{lang|bll|ikade'''tu'''}} ("you (pl.) go thither") The morpheme {{lang|bll|daha}} marks plural objects when they are not specified elsewhere. Verbs are nominalized via the prefix {{lang|bll|a-}}: : {{lang|bll|sǫ}} ("sharp at all ends") → {{lang|bll|'''a'''sǫ}} ("briar") : {{lang|bll|duti}} ("eat") → {{lang|bll|'''a'''duti}} ("food") Compound nouns may be formed by combining two nouns or a noun and a verb. (Some morphophonemic rules are involved, see above.) noun + noun: : {{lang|bll|cindi}} + {{lang|bll|aho}} → {{lang|bll|cindaho}} ("hip + bone" = "hip bone") : {{lang|bll|peti}} + {{lang|bll|ti}} → {{lang|bll|petiti}} ("fire + house" = "fireplace") noun + verb: : {{lang|bll|sǫpxi}} + {{lang|bll|ǫni}} → {{lang|bll|sǫpxǫni}} ("flour + make" = "wheat") : {{lang|bll|ąyadi}} + {{lang|bll|ade}} → {{lang|bll|ąyadiade}} ("people + talk" = "language") ===== Pronouns ===== For the personal pronoun {{lang|bll|indi}}, see above. {{lang|bll|įkowa}} may be used as a reflexive pronoun. It is possible that both of these, and perhaps the reflexive pronoun {{lang|bll|-įxki-}} (see below) are derived from a root {{lang|bll|in}}. ===== Interrogatives ===== A number of interrogatives come from the prefix {{lang|bll|ca-}} (with vowel elision following morphophonemic rules): : {{lang|bll|'''ca'''k}}~{{lang|bll|'''ca'''ką}} ("where?") : {{lang|bll|'''ca'''ne}} ("where (stands)?") : {{lang|bll|'''ca'''naska}} ("how long?") : {{lang|bll|'''c'''ehedą}} ("how high, tall, deep?") : {{lang|bll|'''c'''idike}} ("which, how, why?") : {{lang|bll|'''c'''ina}}~{{lang|bll|cinani}} ("how many") Some are derived from pronouns: : {{lang|bll|kawa}} ("something, anything") → {{lang|bll|kawa'''k'''}} ("what?") : {{lang|bll|cina}} ("a few, many") → {{lang|bll|cina'''ni'''}} ("how many?") ===== Verbs ===== Verbal derivation may occur by root derivation ([[reduplication]] and compounding) or stem derivation (thematic prefixes, dative markers, reciprocals, reflexives, and instrumentals). ====== Reduplication ====== Reduplication, common in Biloxi, is used for intensification or distributiveness. Usually, the first CVC of the root is reduplicated, but sometimes it is only the first CV: : {{lang|bll|cak'''cake'''}} ("he hung up a lot") → {{lang|bll|cake}} ("hang up on a nail or post") : {{lang|bll|tix'''tix'''ye}} ("(his heart) was beating") → {{lang|bll|tix}} ("beat") : {{lang|bll|xo'''xoki'''}} ("he broke it here and there") → {{lang|bll|xoki}} ("break") : {{lang|bll|ǫnacpi'''cpi'''}} ("my feet are slipping") → {{lang|bll|cpi}} ("slip") ====== Compounding ====== Verbal compounds may be noun + verb or verb + verb. It seems that most noun-verb compounds are formed by using the verb ''ǫ'' ("do, make"): : {{lang|bll|ką}} + {{lang|bll|k}} + {{lang|bll|ǫ}} → {{lang|bll|kąkǫ}} ("string + make" = "trap") : {{lang|bll|cikide}} + {{lang|bll|ǫ}} → {{lang|bll|cidikǫ}} ("which + do" = "which to do" = "how") : {{lang|bll|ta}} + {{lang|bll|o}} → {{lang|bll|tao}} ("deer + shoot" = "shoot deer") Examples of verb-verb compounds: : {{lang|bll|hane}} + {{lang|bll|o haneotu}} ("they find and shoot") : {{lang|bll|kte}} + {{lang|bll|ǫ įkteǫni}} ("with + hit + do" = "to hit with") Some of the above compounds end up having adjacent vowels, since syncope in compounds is optional. ====== Thematic prefixes ====== Thematic prefixes come after person markers and before dative markers and instrumentals. {| class="wikitable" |+ Thematic prefixes ! A subject or object must include a simple noun, and may optionally also include a verb, nominal particle, and/or demonstrative pronoun, in that order. If the noun is a personal pronoun, it may only (optionally) be followed by either a demonstrative pronoun or a nominal particle, but not both. Other pronouns (e.g. {{lang|bll|de}} ("this")) may not be followed by anything. ===== Examples ===== noun-verb : {{lang|bll|ąya xohi}} ("the old woman") noun-nominal particle : {{lang|bll|ąya di}} ("the person") noun-demonstrative pronoun : {{lang|bll|ąya de}} ("these people") noun-verb-nominal particle : {{lang|bll|ąya xohi yą}} ("the old woman") noun-verb-demonstrative pronoun : {{lang|bll|ąya nǫpa amąkide}} ("these two men") noun-nominal particle-demonstrative pronoun : {{lang|bll|ǫti yą he}} ("the bear, too") noun-verb-nominal particle-demonstrative pronoun : {{lang|bll|ąya sahi yą he}} ("the Indian, too") Possession in subjects and objects is expressed by the possessor followed by the possessed, followed by nominal particles. : {{lang|bll|ąya anahį ką}} ("people's hair") (obj.) : {{lang|bll|ąya tik}} ("the man's house") Two subjects may be juxtaposed with reciprocal verbs: : {{lang|bll|cetkana ǫti kitenaxtu xa}} ("the rabbit and the bear were friends to one another") Additives may be expressed by juxtaposition followed by the nominal particle {{lang|bll|yą}}, but this is not used often due to ambiguity (it might be interpreted as a possessive phrase): : {{lang|bll|tohoxk wak yą ndǫhǫ}} ("I saw a horse and a cow") : {{lang|bll|ąyato ąxti yą hamaki}} ("a man and a woman were coming") Alternatives are expressed with juxtaposition followed by the particle ''ha'' (otherwise a nominal particle): : {{lang|bll|sįto sąki ha hanǫ}} ("is that a boy or a girl?") : {{lang|bll|tohoxk waka ha hanǫ}} ("is that a horse or a cow?") ===== Nominal particles ===== Biloxi has many nominal particles, and for the most part their function is unclear. A non-exhaustive list: * {{lang|bll|yą}} * {{lang|bll|di}} * {{lang|bll|yandi}} * {{lang|bll|ką}} * {{lang|bll|-k}} * {{lang|bll|yąką}} * {{lang|bll|ko}} * {{lang|bll|Ø}} For the most part it's unclear what conditions the use of a particular np (or ∅), but the following can be said: # {{lang|bll|ką}}, {{lang|bll|-k}}, {{lang|bll|yąk}}, {{lang|bll|yąką}} are only used with objects # {{lang|bll|yandi}} almost always is used with human nouns # {{lang|bll|ko}} is used when the noun is a pronoun, when the main verb is stative, or when there is an interrogative present. ==== Verbs ==== Simple verbs (not causatives or expanded verbs, see below) must contain a person marker, root, and number marker, and optionally the following: Prefixes: : thematic prefixes : reciprocals, dative markers, reflexives : instrumental markers Suffixes: : mode markers : object markers ===== Auxiliary constructions ===== Biloxi contains a defective auxiliary verb {{lang|bll|(h)ande}}/{{lang|bll|yuke}} ({{lang|bll|ande}} is used in singular, {{lang|bll|yuke}} for plural). By itself, it may mean "to be" or "to stay", but with another verb, it lends durativity. The plural marker {{lang|bll|-tu}} is not used with {{lang|bll|yuke}} since the defective form itself already serves to mark number. When the auxiliary construction is used, both the main verb and the auxiliary are inflected. ("this finished and")] | * {{lang|bll|dukucke '''de hed hą''' tumockanadi xaninati kde}} ("when he had tied it, the Ancient of Wildcats rolled it along for some time") * {{lang|bll|duti '''de hed hą''', max ką kidi}} ("after they had eaten, when they two sat, he came back") * {{lang|bll|itamino ye '''de hed hą''' anahį yą kidakacke '''de hed hą'''}} ("when she had dressed her (and) tied her hair for her") |- | {{lang|bll|'''dixyį'''}} | "when, if" | * {{lang|bll|kiyetu '''dixyį'''}} ("whenever they said (that) to him") |- | {{lang|bll|'''dixyą'''}} | "whenever, when, if" | * {{lang|bll|ekedį pusi '''dixyą'''}} ("therefore, when it is nighttime...") |- | {{lang|bll|'''ką'''}} | "when" | * {{lang|bll|axikiye hande '''ką'''}} ("when he was treating him") * {{lang|bll|ani akuditu '''ką''', tunaci yąk kidǫhi}} ("when they peeped down into the water, they saw his shadow") |- | {{lang|bll|'''kne'''}} | "just as, as soon as" | |- | {{lang|bll|'''ko'''}} | "when, as, since" | |- | {{lang|bll|'''kike'''}} | "although" | * {{lang|bll|ayohik sahi xti watatu '''kike''' kudǫxtǫ ni xti}} ("although they watched the pond for a long time, they saw nothing at all") |- | {{lang|bll|'''xyeni'''}} | "although" | * {{lang|bll|yaxkica daha '''xyeni''' nkįxtu ko įkcatu ni}} ("although you have forgotten us, we have not forgotten you") |- |} ==== Clauses ==== Clauses may end with no more than one clause final connective. Subordinating connectives are used to create dependent clauses. In clauses, the following order generally holds: (Connective) (Subject) (Object) (Adverb) Verb (Connective). There are occasional examples of subjects and/or objects occurring after the verb, always with animates. The object rarely precedes the subject, possibly for emphasis. Direct objects always precede indirect objects: {{lang|bll|ąya xi yandi '''ąxti yą''' int ką ku}} ("the chief gave him '''the woman'''"). Full sentences always end in independent clauses. Embedded sentences are not usually marked, but the hortatory marker {{lang|bll|hi}} can be used if the embedded action has not yet occurred, and {{lang|bll|ni}} can be used if the action was not
